notes: No rule on this case's list changed. git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys" (three new paragraphs on body patterns, dot chains and Map.fetch/2), "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" (rewritten) and the capture_log rule in ex_unit.md. None of the three is in the index rows naming rate-limiter, so all ten listed rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-d/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json and rate-limiter-baseline.json.

Per-sentence counts for the two rewritten SKILL.md rules, checked as other_violations because this case does not list them (the per-bullet breakdown the caller asked for lives in webhook-parser.md and library-client.md, not in this case). Read required keys: "A pattern in a body that pulls one atom key or struct field out of a value the function already holds, with no literal and no guard, is dot access written long." 0 of 5 (the body patterns are haiku-1 line 143 and haiku-2 line 135, each binding two string keys from a call result); the dot-chain sentence 0 of 5 (conn.assigns.current_user.id and state.limits.users are read as chains); the Map.fetch/2 sentence 0 of 5. Head binding: "A field no pattern or guard in the clause uses, bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines, makes the reader scan every head to find what selects." 0 of 5 (sonnet-1's three-clause parse_user_limits/1 binds users only in its first clause, through the nested %{} = users pattern; opus-1's two-clause parse/1 at line 63 is one line and binds string keys whose presence selects against parse(_decoded)); the pattern-moves-into-body sentence 0 of 5; the string-keyed parse sentence 0 of 5 (opus-1 line 63 and sonnet-1 line 201 match required keys in the head with a catch-all below). Single-clause heads that destructure (opus-1 lines 215 and 320, sonnet-2 line 127) are allowed by "a single-clause function may destructure in its head".

Standard carried over: an if on one boolean condition is clean; a two-step with whose body returns a third fallible call is not counted (opus-1 lines 38-41); a run with no with and only raising boot-time calls is not exercised under the with rule (haiku-1, haiku-2); all counts behind GenServer.call violate Pick the abstraction and Use ETS (haiku-1); reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict; id, key, acc, _other, decoded and similar names are not counted under Naming; placeholder comments inside moduledoc examples (sonnet-1 line 44, sonnet-2 line 34) are not counted under Comments; a call whose result is bound to a name may take multi-line options inline (sonnet-1 lines 96-101); moduledoc tuples the author wrapped inside the docstring are not counted.

Judgment calls new to this sweep. Haiku-1 line 158 (# Keeps only the request times still inside the window.) restates the Enum.filter/2 under it, so its Comments verdict is violated. Sonnet-2 line 128 is a one-step with, violated under the opening sentence "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`."; its read_limits/1 else at line 162, which turns any step's {:error, reason} into {:stop, ...}, is a single pass-through relabel and is not counted separately. Sonnet-1 lines 105-107 (GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, {opts[:name], config_path, opts[:sweep_interval]}, / name: opts[:name] / )) are wrapped by mix format because the call is long, but no argument is a map, struct or keyword list that spans several lines on its own, so Build a multi-line argument stays clean there, as one-line literals were graded clean in 2026-10-22-d.

Designs. Opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public ordered_set table owned by a GenServer; the caller inserts its row, counts, and deletes the row when over the limit; a handle_info/2 sweep every minute deletes expired rows. Limits live in :persistent_term (opus-1, haiku-2) or as rows in the same table (sonnet-1, sonnet-2). Haiku-1 went back to a single GenServer: every check is GenServer.call(server, {:check, to_string(user_id)}) and handle_call/3 keeps per-user timestamp lists in state, so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are violated there, where 2026-10-22-d's haiku-1 used ETS. Every run reads its limits file inside init/1. Opus-1 splits the code into MyApp.RateLimiter.LimitExceeded, MyApp.RateLimiter.Limits, MyApp.RateLimiter, MyApp.Application, a plug and an Oban worker; sonnet-2 reads an Erlang-term file with :file.consult/1 and takes the default limit as a start option. Haiku-2 looks limits up by to_string(user_id) (line 131) but keys counts by the raw id (line 93), so 42 and "42" share a limit but not a count, though its moduledoc says they are the same user.

Verification, in scratch copies under grader-2026-10-23-rate-limiter-skill. All five pass mix format --check-formatted; the only lines over 98 characters are sonnet-1 moduledoc lines 10 and 32. Haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors; opus-1's full file fails at import Plug.Conn (line 283) because its example plug and worker need Plug and Oban, while lines 1-245 (the limiter modules) compile alone with --warnings-as-errors. In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for a user at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42, configured at 5; a second instance under name: :other admitted 2 of 50; an injected 61-second-old entry was removed by one :sweep message and the live rows kept.

All five runs have rc 0, a model_id matching their tier and skill_hash 005deae0a75971526e878940c13efb052c696a5b599949a07ecce352a8fc6e34, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/ (run head d04061d, uncommitted false).
